subject: Post-call recap: trial runbook, orchestration and eval routing
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-call recap: trial runbook, orchestration and eval routing

Hi Caroline — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a proposed runbook so we can get aligned on scope, timelines and how we'll measure success. I copied Vanessa (Success) and Neha (Solutions) to own handoffs.

High-level objective
- Validate Redwood inference for MedLink triage workflows (clinical note classification + routing) at production-like scale while safeguarding PHI.

Proposed 3-stage trial runbook (high level)
1) Data onboarding & offline baseline (1–2 weeks)
   - Sanitize and transfer a 2k–5k sample set (de-identified) for offline eval.
   - Redwood runs offline scoring against rubric to baseline precision/recall.
2) Shadow deployment (2–4 weeks)
   - Live traffic shadow (no action) for latency, throughput, and distribution shift checks.
   - Observability hooks enabled (traces, token counts, KV cache profiles).
3) Acceptance & limited live (1 week)
   - Canary routing to 5–10% users with rollback triggers; success sign-off by MedLink.

Success criteria (proposed) — need your sign-off
- Precision@1 >= 0.88 on offline labeled set
- Recall on priority classes >= 0.80
- Latency p95 <= 300ms (in-region GPU) during shadow
- No critical safety/regulatory flags in 1000 sampled predictions

Eval methodology and grading rubric (short)
- Offline labeled set: primary quality gate (metrics above).
- Shadow online: operational gate (latency, token costs, error rate, QA spot-check pass rate).
- Composite pass rule: must pass both offline quality and shadow operational gates OR else we iterate on prompts/quantization for a single rollback/adjust cycle.

Ownership & roles
- Redwood SE (Neha) — data ingest, eval instrumentation, tuning support
- Redwood Success (Vanessa) — acceptance coordination, SOW sign-off
- MedLink PM (Caroline) — dataset provision, labeling coordinator, acceptance owner

Immediate asks / next steps
- Caroline: confirm data availability window and whether legal can sign the trial SOW this week.
- MedLink: share SOC2 contact if your security team wants to run the questionnaire (we attached the questionnaire).
- Redwood: schedule kickoff — tentative 2026-09-08 (Jonas to Doodle)

Attachments: trial-runbook-draft-v1.pdf, eval-rubric.xlsx, security-questionnaire.pdf

If that looks good I'll turn this into a one-page runbook and drop a DocuSign SOW link.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber

Caroline — quick technical clarifications and concrete proposal from the SE side. Quoting your note above for context:

> "Can you confirm estimated cost for the shadow (approx GPU hours)"

Short answers:
- Offline eval dataset recommended sizes: 2,000–5,000 labeled examples across priority classes; if labeling budget is constrained we can do a stratified 1,000 sample and bootstrap metrics.
- Shadow run cost: depends on traffic. For light traffic (~10 requests/min) we estimate ~30–60 GPU hours/week on a single dedicated instance; for production-like throughput we should assume 200–400 GPU hours/week. We'll provide a cost estimate doc once you confirm expected QPS during the shadow window.

Shadow vs offline eval — instrumentation details
- Shadow: real traffic duplicated to Redwood (no external side effects). We'll mask PHI at ingest and store only telemetry and hashed identifiers. Shadow lets us measure p95 latency, tail behavior, and cache hit rates across sequences.
- Offline: allows fine-grained labeling and edge-case QA (we'll compute precision/recall, top-K accuracy, and annotated failure modes).

Scoring / grading rubric (proposed columns included in attached eval-rubric.xlsx):
- Quality: Precision@1, Recall (per-class), F1 on priority cohorts
- Operational: Latency p95, Error % (exceptions), Token cost per request
- Safety: Rate of flagged outputs per 1k (manual review sample)

Pass thresholds (initial proposal)
- Precision@1 >= 0.88; Recall >= 0.80 on priority classes; Latency p95 <= 300ms; Safety flags < 1 per 1k samples

Operational ownership (detailed)
- Data ingest checklist (attached) — MedLink provides export, Redwood validates schema, then SE runs ingestion scripts.
- Vanessa: coordinate acceptance sign-offs and runbook ops.

Attachments: data_ingest_checklist.xlsx, eval-rubric.xlsx

Will prepare a short cost estimate and a one-page tech runbook for kickoff.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
